correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge2\), peeling matching-pair first colour classes until the first same-side second occurrence gives the exact event \(\{X\ge t+2\}\). Distinct ordered selections of t pairs give disjoint linear-extension sets of a two-chain precedence poset. Base \(L_{n,1}=(2n)!/n^2\) and explicit earliest-two/three case split \(L_{n,t}=3L_{n-1,t-1}\) yield each factorial tail; all edge cases (\(n=2\), \(t=n-2\)) are handled. Differences and tail sums yield the law, mean, and count of worst orders. C++17 exhaustive simulations checked 3,669,864 vertex orders for \(2\le n\le5\); independent subset-DP checked all 28 poset cases at \(3\le n\le9\). Finite computations supplement the displayed infinite proof and do not replace it.

value.rationale: This gives the complete all-colour distribution, not merely a moment or bound, for a canonical online-colouring worst-case graph under the important random-arrival model. It converts the known upper mean \(2.5+O(1/n)\) to exact finite-n expressions with mean tending sharply to 2 at rate \(1/n\), determines a rare-event tail to the maximum \(n\) colours and gives an explicit factor-three linear-extension mechanism explaining random-order behavior. The result supplies general structural information not recoverable from previously published simulations, and is motivated by precisely the crown family singled out in the source literature.
